author: Mark Manson
description:

If confidence comes from real evidence, then where does self-esteem fit, and why did an entire generation get it so wrong? In chapter four, Drew and I take a detour into the self-esteem movement, the feel-good experiment that promised to fix everything from crime to school performance and ended up backfiring in ways we're still living with. We get into the California task force that staked millions on proving self-esteem was a social cure-all, why praising kids for who they are instead of what they do breeds fragility and even narcissism rather than real confidence, and the William James insight the whole movement misread. Then we get to the useful part: how you actually build the kind of confidence that generalizes across your life.
